query: What is the date of birth of the English inventor that developed the Richard Hornsby & Sons oil engine?

pipeline_result.response: The date of birth of the English inventor that developed the Hornsby-Akroyd oil engine is 4 June 1790.
retrieved_context: Richard Hornsby: Richard Hornsby Elsham in Lincolnshire 4 June 1790 - 1864. was an inventor and founder of a major agricultural machinery firm that developed steam engines.  His firm also developed early diesels and caterpillar tracks.  He lived with a farming family, the son of William Hornsby and his wife Sarah.

Richard Hornsby & Sons: Richard Hornsby & Sons was an engine and machinery manufacturer in Lincolnshire, England from 1828 until 1918.  The company was a pioneer in the manufacture of the oil engine developed by Herbert Akroyd Stuart, which was marketed under the "Hornsby-Akroyd" name.  The company developed an early track system for vehicles, selling the patent to Holt & Co. (predecessor to Caterpillar Inc.) in America.  In 1918, Richard Hornsby & Sons became a subsidiary of the neighbouring engineering firm Rustons of Lincoln, to create "Ruston & Hornsby".

Hornsby-Akroyd oil engine: The Hornsby-Akroyd oil engine was the first successful design of internal combustion engine using "heavy oil" as a fuel.  It was the first to use a separate vapourising combustion chamber and is the forerunner of all hot-bulb engines.
